name: read_attachment
description:
Reads a file a person attached to a message in this conversation. Each attachment appears in the message as a line naming its ID, file name, type, and size. Images are shown to you. Text files come back as numbered lines: a line number, then a tab, then the line, numbered from 1. By default it reads up to 2000 lines from the start; offset and limit read another stretch of a long file. Other files, such as PDFs, archives, and videos, are only described. To work on the file with your own tools, pass path to save a copy on your machine; relative paths start from your working directory, and missing folders are created. Choose a place that will not get committed, such as an ignored scratch folder. An existing file is replaced only with overwrite: true. The copy is yours: changing or deleting it does not change the attachment, and you can save it again.

Search keywords: attached file, open attachment, uploaded file, read attachment.

path.description: Where to save a copy of the file on your machine, relative to your working directory or absolute. Omit it to only look at the file.

overwrite.description: Replace a file that already exists at path. Defaults to false.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.
